messages:
Alex_Support: Heads up — Acme private cluster started seeing TLS errors to our endpoint after a cert rotation ~45m ago. Internal apps get 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Some clients succeed. Repro: curl from app pod fails, external tests OK.
Maria_Eng: Thanks — can you paste curl + openssl s_client output? Any pattern which AZ or node? Were intermediates rotated too?
Alex_Support: Repro outputs below. Trying from two different IPs returned by internal DNS.
```bash
# failing IP
curl -v --resolve api.acme.internal:443:10.3.8.54 https://api.acme.internal/health
* Connected to api.acme.internal (10.3.8.54) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Closing connection 0

# openssl
openssl s_client -connect 10.3.8.54:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Acme-Leaf-CA
---
Server certificate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
---
no client certificate CA names sent
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
```
Alex_Support: Same check to 10.3.8.12 succeeds (server sends full chain, verify=OK).
Jay_Infra: We rotated leaf & intermediate last night and pushed new bundle. Rotator logged success for most nodes. Could be a node that missed update or is serving an old bundle from disk cache. Are clients hitting different IPs? Check DNS TTL and A records.
Alex_Support: Internal DNS (consul) returns two A records for api.acme.internal: 10.3.8.12 and 10.3.8.54. curl to .12 -> 200, to .54 -> cert verify fail.
Priya_SRE: Noted — we also had alerts earlier about failed outbound connections to ocsp.acme-ca.com from AZ-b. If OCSP stapling fails or OCSP check cannot reach responder and client policy is strict, that can cause failures. Can we get openssl s_client -status output?
Alex_Support: Ran -status against both IPs:
```bash
openssl s_client -connect 10.3.8.54:443 -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
No OCSP response sent
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Acme-Leaf-CA
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---

openssl s_client -connect 10.3.8.12:443 -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
OCSP Response: Good
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Acme-Leaf-CA
 1 s:/CN=Acme-Intermediate
   i:/CN=Acme-Root
---
verify return:1
---
```
Alex_Support: TL;DR: .54 serving only leaf cert (missing intermediate) and no OCSP stapling; .12 has full chain + OCSP stapling.
Maria_Eng: Looks like two issues: 1) node .54 didn't get updated chain (or serves stale bundle), 2) OCSP stapling failing from that AZ due to egress block. Jay, can you check rotator logs and the post-rotate hook for .54?
Jay_Infra: Rotator shows bundle push succeeded but post-rotate hook that hits our internal webhook `https://inframanager.internal/ack` returned 504 for .54 at 2026-03-16T09:18:05Z. That webhook call goes over VPC egress to management subnet; there was a deny rule applied by a recent firewall change that hit AZ-b instances. I can manually push the full chain to .54 and restart the rotate agent. Also opening firewall to allow inframanager traffic.
Alex_Support: After manual push, re-ran test: openssl now shows full chain and OCSP stapling present on .54. Customer reported errors stopped ~2m after we fixed .54.
Priya_SRE: We also found that ocsp.acme-ca.com (13.224.55.1/32) was not in the egress allowlist for the AZ-b subnet due to a typo in the template. That caused intermittent failures contacting OCSP responders. I've added the IP to the egress ACL and validated outbound TCP 80/443 to the responder.
Maria_Eng: Good catch. Action items:
- Audit rotation post-hooks for egress dependencies and make them resilient (retries/backoff).
- Add OCSP responder IPs to default egress allowlist templates.
- Run a consistency check across nodes to detect missing intermediates and force-rotate any mismatches.
- Adjust proxy cache TTLs (see Priya's note) to avoid serving stale DNS-to-IP mappings after rotation.
Priya_SRE: Additional detail: our proxy cache was set to 300s which allowed the old mapping to persist; changed proxy cache TTL to 60s and flushed service caches. Added alert to cert-checker: "missing-intermediate-chain" when verify error:num=20 observed.
Alex_Support: I'll follow up with Acme CE with remediation summary and ETA for a short postmortem. Thanks everyone.
Deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: rotation-fix-hotpatch rolled to 10.3.8.54 at 2026-03-16T09:35:12Z
